content_sections.heading: About DLSA Balrampur
content_sections.text: The District Legal Services Authority, Balrampur runs the legal services programmes of the National Legal Services Authority, New Delhi and the State Legal Services Authority in Balrampur district, Uttar Pradesh. The PLVs are being engaged on the instructions of the District Judge, Shri Utkarsh Chaturvedi, to publicise these programmes and help carry them out. The notice is signed by Yashpal Verma, Secretary of the Authority.

content_sections.heading: DLSA Balrampur Para-Legal Volunteer Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: The official notification does not specify the minimum educational qualification. Instead, it invites applications from people in these groups: Doctors and teachers (retired) Government servants and senior citizens (retired) MSW students and teachers Anganwadi workers Members of the transgender community Law students, until they are enrolled as advocates Representatives and workers of voluntary organisations Members of women's organisations, Maitri Sangathan and other service groups Educated prisoners with good conduct serving long sentences in jail. The Superintendent of the District Jail will tell prisoners about this notice and forward their applications to the DLSA office by the due date. Specially talented sportspersons and distinguished artists Exceptional and talented people who have shown notable skill in any field Any other person the District Authority considers suitable Preference: preference goes to people who want to bring legal services to the public, care about poor and weaker sections of society, and want to help them develop and move up socially. Each person may submit only one application. For the exact eligibility of each category, see the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Honorarium and Duties
content_sections.text: PLVs are paid an honorarium for each working day at the rate fixed by the National/State Legal Services Authority. It is paid for set tasks: visiting remote villages, handing out legal literacy material, and working at the Legal Aid Clinic and the Front Office.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: The Authority will look at the applications it receives and then hold an interview on 30 October 2026 at the District and Sessions Court, Balrampur. No travel allowance is paid for attending the interview.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for DLSA Balrampur Para-Legal Volunteer Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Get the application form from the office of the District Legal Services Authority, Balrampur, or download it from the website of the District Court (Janpad Nyayalay), Balrampur. Fill in the form. Only one application is allowed per person. Send it by registered post or hand it in by 4:00 PM on 29 October 2026. Submit it at either of these: Office of the District Legal Services Authority, Balrampur Office of the Tehsil Legal Services Committee at Balrampur (Sadar), Utraula or Tulsipur Prisoners send their applications through the Superintendent of the District Jail, Balrampur. For any other information, contact the DLSA office in Balrampur during office hours on any working day.

faq.question: Q1. How many Para-Legal Volunteers will DLSA Balrampur select?
faq.answer: 17 in all: 8 at the district headquarters, 5 at Tehsil Sadar Balrampur, and 2 each at Tehsil Utraula and Tehsil Tulsipur.

faq.question: Q2. What time on the last day is the deadline?
faq.answer: Applications must reach the office by 4:00 PM on 29 October 2026.

faq.question: Q3. Where can I submit the form?
faq.answer: At the District Legal Services Authority office in Balrampur, or at the Tehsil Legal Services Committee office in Balrampur (Sadar), Utraula or Tulsipur. You can send it by registered post or hand it in yourself.

faq.question: Q4. Where do I get the application form?
faq.answer: From the District Legal Services Authority office in Balrampur, or as a download from the District Court, Balrampur website.

faq.question: Q5. When and where is the interview?
faq.answer: On 30 October 2026 at the District and Sessions Court, Balrampur. No travel allowance is paid for attending.

faq.question: Q6. Can law students apply?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as they are not yet enrolled as advocates.

faq.question: Q7. How are PLVs paid?
faq.answer: They receive an honorarium for each working day, at the rate set by the National/State Legal Services Authority. It covers tasks such as visiting remote villages, handing out legal literacy material, and working at the Legal Aid Clinic and Front Office.

faq.question: Q8. Can prisoners apply?
faq.answer: Yes. Educated prisoners with good conduct who are serving long sentences can apply. The Superintendent of the District Jail forwards their applications to the DLSA office.

faq.question: Q9. Can I send more than one application?
faq.answer: No. Each person may submit only one application.
